thick bakery style chocolate chip cookies🍪🍫 Ingredients: 170g (3/4 cup) unsalted butter, cold and cubed 150g (3/4 cup) brown sugar 70g (1/3 cup) granulated sugar 1 egg + 1 egg yolk 2 tsp vanilla 300g (2 1/2 cups) all purpose flour 1 tbsp cornstarch 1/2 tsp baking soda 1/4 tsp baking powder 3/4 tsp salt 250g (1 1/2 cups) chocolate chips  Flakey sea salt (optional) Instructions:  1. In a large bowl, combine the butter, brown sugar, and white sugar. Mix until smooth and well combined. Do not cream. 2. Add the egg, egg yolk, and vanilla, then mix until fully incorporated. 3. Add the dry ingredients (flour, cornstarch, baking powder, baking soda, and salt) and fold until just combined. 4. Fold in the chocolate chips or chunks until evenly distributed. Do not overmix. 5. Divide the dough into 150g portions and shape each into a rough ball. 6. Place the dough balls on a lined tray, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight. 7. Bake in a preheated 190°C (375°F) oven for 13-16 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the centers are still slightly soft. 8. Allow the cookies to cool on the baking tray for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack. If desired, sprinkle with flaky sea salt and let cool for about 15 minutes before serving. Enjoy! Note: This recipe made 6 cookies weighing 150g each and 1 cookie weighing 100g🍪🤎 #baking #cookies #chocolatechipcookies #Recipe #nyccookies

In a pan, melt butter over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté until fragrant. Add Kewpie mayo, Buldak sauce, and powder packet. Mix well until it turns thick and glossy. Add chili oil and stir. Pour in heavy cream and mix until smooth, creamy, and slightly thickened (that rich orange color 🔥). Add noodles and toss until fully coated. Sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top and let it melt into the sauce. Add dumplings and sausages on top. Cover and let everything heat through. Set aside. Boil the Buldak noodles according to the package instructions. When the noodles are halfway cooked, drain most of the water, leaving a little in the pan. Let it simmer for about 1 minute so the noodles absorb all the flavor. Add mozzarella cheese and let it melt into the ramen until extra cheesy and creamy. Dumbbell Sumo Squat  Know the difference  1. Dumbbell Position Hold the dumbbell with both hands naturally hanging between your legs, rather than holding it at your chest. This allows you to lift heavier weights without being limited by arm strength. 2. Torso Posture Maintain a slight forward lean instead of staying fully upright. Leaning forward increases hip flexion, helping to stretch and better activate the glutes. 3. Stance Width and Foot Angle Set your feet about 1.5 times shoulder-width apart, with your toes pointing outward at roughly a 45-degree angle. If the stance is too wide, the inner thigh muscles (adductors) will take over, reducing glute activation. 4. Load Path As you squat down, the dumbbell should not stay directly under your shoulders. Instead, it should fall slightly behind the midline, closer to your posterior chain. Bring your hands slightly inward to keep the load closer to your center of mass, which helps reduce lower back strain and improves movement efficiency. #gymtips #quads #gluteworkout #gym #gymrat
